normative_extracts.quote: A service worker has an associated state, which is one of parsed, installing, installed, activating, activated, or redundant.
Until all pages controlled by the previous service worker are closed, the new worker remains in the waiting state unless skipWaiting() is invoked.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: Runs an event-driven worker thread decoupled from any DOM tab that intercepts origin fetches and enforces single-version tab ownership until old clients unload.

production_failures.symptom: Users stuck on broken mixed-version app after deploy (old HTML + new chunk URLs or vice versa)
production_failures.root_cause: Calling self.skipWaiting() unconditionally caused the new service worker to take over an already-loaded tab whose DOM referenced old asset hashes.
production_failures.mitigation: Prompt the user to reload when a waiting worker is detected, or ensure all chunk URLs are content-hashed and retained across overlapping deploys.

production_failures.symptom: Service worker update never installs even after deploying new code
production_failures.root_cause: sw.js itself was served with Cache-Control: max-age=86400 or its byte-for-byte contents didn't change.
production_failures.mitigation: Serve sw.js with Cache-Control: no-cache (or max-age=0) so the browser always revalidates the worker script on navigation.
